What do these columns mean?
Betthe side we like: O/U a win line, Yes/No otherwise
Marketthe market's chance for that side (its Kalshi price), with American odds
Modelour chance for that side, with fair odds
Edge¢model minus market after fees, in cents
eROIexpected return: edge ÷ the price paid
Best Betstight, well-traded books, 25%+ eROI, 3¢+ edge after fees; Liquid = the busiest books; Clear = every market, no filters
Take $ / +2¢ $dollars you could buy on the bet side at the listed price, and paying up to 2¢ more (from the order book, before fees)
Advanced viewthe book (Bid / Ask), the Take $ columns and the maker numbers - resting 1¢ inside the book, after its own (often lower) fee; blank where the book is too wide to rest in

Heisman projections · stats and Kalshi prices as of Sep 26, 1:30 AM CT · 55 candidates · 2% left for a winner outside this list
What is this?
# the Blend's order - the table opens sorted by it
Player / Team his position beside his name; beside his team its rank in the Power Ratings (the PWR chip, 1 = the best team in FBS) and its record so far; click a team for its card
Proj Rec his team's projected regular-season record: expected wins - expected losses, to one decimal
QBR / EPA how efficient his season has been so far. A quarterback's Total QBR: a 0-100 grade of every play he makes - passing, running, sacks and fumbles - adjusted for the defenses faced (50 = average, 90+ = elite; Heisman-winning quarterbacks finished around 90). A back's or receiver's EPA per play: the expected points his plays added, not adjusted for the defense - receivers run higher than backs (a catch, not a carry), so each is colored against his own position. Hover for his percentile among FBS players of his position
Proj TD / Yds touchdowns and yards he is projected to be responsible for over the full season, title game included - passing, rushing and receiving together (the split on hover)
Model our chance he wins the Heisman when ballots close (after the conference title games), from simulating the rest of the season and how Heisman voters have picked winners in the past. Part of the chance is left for a winner outside this list (the line above the table)
Score the Heisman Score: our overall grade of his case at ballot time, 0-100 with 50 = the average candidate here (most winners scored 98+ - Past Winners). Tap a player for what goes into it
Blend our chance combined with the Kalshi price, with its American odds. One forecast among others, never a sure edge
Finalist his chance of being one of the four finalists invited to New York, with its American odds
Kalshi what a taker pays to buy YES right now - the ask plus Kalshi's fee - in cents (hover for bid / ask and the NO side)
Edge / eROI the better side for a taker now at our Blend chance, after fees: YES +4.9¢ = a YES bought now is worth 4.9¢ more than it costs; none = neither side pays. eROI = that edge over the price paid (grey when neither side pays)
More columns adds his position, his team's record as a column of its own, its power rating (points better than an average FBS team on a neutral field), efficiency (passer rating for a quarterback, yards per touch for the rest), his team's projected losses and those against unranked teams, his rank by the Model, and American odds beside the Model and the Kalshi price. Show current stats adds the same stats so far, and the Score and win chance if the season ended today
Colors shaded against past Heisman finalists and winners when ballots closed: no color at an ordinary candidate's level, green from a lower finalist's level to full at a typical winner's (QBR against past quarterbacks; touchdowns, yards and efficiency against his position; team power, projected record and the rating; losses the other way), red below the average candidate. An unbeaten record shades green as the season goes on; the chances only shade green (the finalist chance from 20%); a positive edge shades green. Hover a column header for what it means
Tip click a player's row for his card - each stat now → projected at ballot time, bars for what he has banked of his projected touchdowns and yards, his Score and his chances (a small part of a total - a receiver's few carries - counts but is not listed); click a team for its card; click any column header to sort by it (again to reverse)
